description: We're Ctrl+Space, a beginner-friendly team exploring creative space-tech ideas through NASA Space Apps 2026.
summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions.

Through an engaging web-based archive, the project brings attention to spacecraft, scientific instruments, rovers, and other equipment that contributed to our understanding of these worlds. Instead of treating them as forgotten objects, the website presents them as historical artifacts with stories of exploration, scientific discovery, and technological achievement.

With interactive storytelling, visual exploration, and educational elements, the project aims to make planetary exploration history accessible and interesting, particularly for younger audiences.

By preserving the stories behind these objects, Abandoned but Not Forgotten encourages people to appreciate the legacy of space exploration and recognize that even equipment no longer in operation can hold scientific and historical significance.
details:
Project Overview

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive website that explores the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. The idea is to bring attention to these often-overlooked objects and the role they played in helping us understand other worlds.

How It Works

The website takes visitors through an interactive exploration of the Moon and Mars. They can discover different pieces of equipment, learn about the missions they belonged to, understand why they were sent, and explore the stories behind them.

Rather than simply presenting facts and mission details, we use visual storytelling and interactive elements to make the information more interesting and easier to understand.

Benefits and Intended Impact

We want people to look beyond the successful missions and remember the equipment that made those achievements possible. Even though some of these objects are no longer operational, they still have scientific and historical importance.

Through this project, we hope to make space exploration history more engaging, encourage curiosity about the Moon and Mars, and help people appreciate the legacy of human exploration beyond Earth.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code as our development environment. Netlify was used to host the website, and NASA's publicly available resources were used for research and mission information.

Creativity and Design

We wanted to present this topic in a way that feels more like exploring a digital space archive than reading a collection of historical facts. The interactive Moon and Mars experience allows visitors to discover the objects and their stories at their own pace.

Our main focus was to combine space history, education, and storytelling in a simple and engaging way, giving attention to the equipment that often gets overlooked when we talk about space exploration.
